answer: Ferrous Inter-Arrival Fingerprinting. Each identity’s first N actions must arrive with inter-arrival timing drawn from a heavy-tailed distribution; enforcement compares the empirical hazard curve to a cedar-calibrated baseline and flags identities whose traffic is too regular. Sybils spun up in bulk emit machine-regular bursts, so mimicking organic jitter forces attackers to pace each identity across a karst of slow, randomized delays—paying wall-clock time and scheduling overhead per identity, not just registration cost.
